posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text:
DDHQ FORECAST UPDATE (10/26): Senate

Democrats have a 57% chance of flipping the Senate.

Democrats need to flip four seats; they lead in five (Alaska, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas) in our forecast. https://t.co/uPU9UEPnfO

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text:
DDHQ FORECAST UPDATE (10/26): House

Democrats now have a 79% chance of flipping the House.

With a forecasted advantage in 238 seats, Democrats are at their widest lead of the cycle. 

10 seats remain in the Toss Up column. https://t.co/vB9Qgh2wEd

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text:
Likely Republican -> Leans Republican

Our latest Senate forecast has shifted towards Independent Dan Osborn.

Republican Pete Ricketts remains the favorite, with a 73% win probability, but polls remain tight. https://t.co/4Nk2zpaTxd

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: There's some difference of opinion re: Nov. 3, but less than most cycles in the past. Even the most optimistic non-insane Rs are like, "All these Senate races are toss-ups." Even the most optimistic non-insane Ds are like "We like our odds, but we'll believe it when we see it."

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: Democrats aren't going to underperform by 7 points among likely voters relative to registered voters, especially in a year where D turnout is likely to be fairly high by every available measure. Jackson +9 also seems unlikely, but this is two wrongs making a (maybe?) right. https://t.co/jlLDijBNP4

posts.name: Dave Wasserman
posts.text: Think back to 2006, last midterm w/ an unpopular war/GOP president. Where were the biggest House upsets? Places like IN, IA, KS, MN (Tim Walz!), NH, OH, WI, Upstate NY. That's why I think the Midwest & places w/ lots of secular white voters are especially ripe for surprises.

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: I'm not sure what it would take to de-entrench the presumption that polls systematically underrate conservative parties or candidates. It's not true historically, but it's a cheapie take that will never really get you criticized.

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: The gap between FLIPR and prediction markets is closing, but I thought some of you would appreciate a column that goes into detail about the disagreements. It comes down to state-by-state differences of opinion, rather than anything overly "macro".

posts.name: G Elliott Morris
posts.text: We don't know if the early vote will be predictive bc all Reps could just be waiting to vote until Elec Day. What this means in practice is that to win, the GOP will have to have the most successful EDay mobilization operation in modern history.
